scope: Review only: menus, navigation, visual hierarchy and player journeys. No menu implementation changes.

method.fresh: Native Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility captures at 1280x720 and 960x540, isolated workspace APPDATA, BMT_API_URL disabled.
method.retained: Inspected dated native evidence for Garage, achievements, Trackside, Rivalry, challenges, results and publication confirmation. Fixture identities and outcomes are presentation examples.
limitations: Heuristic expert assessment; no player usability study.
No phone attachment check or physical-device testing.
No live sign-in, purchases, races, publication, account mutation or deployment.
Older screenshot details superseded by current source were excluded from findings.
No FPS, retention or conversion measurements.

assessment: The visual identity is recognisable and several screens are well composed. The largest opportunities are mode discovery, first-race guidance, state communication and consistency across feature destinations.
preserve: Dark navy/off-white/yellow palette and condensed display type.
Real-car Garage and independent car preview/confirmation.
Scenic biome previews and route silhouettes.
Simplified achievement title bar and content-fitting detail sheets.
Normal race summary before competition-specific feedback.

findings.title: Label essential mode navigation
findings.observed: Race modes are icon-only and named through hover tooltips; unavailable Friends uses much the same presentation. Garage rail contents change after car confirmation.
findings.impact: First-time touch players must infer destinations and may mistake unavailable controls for available ones.
findings.recommendation: Keep the approved rail locations; add compact persistent captions or a clear expanded state, and communicate availability. Preserve stable positions for common destinations.

findings.title: Lead the first session toward racing
findings.observed: New local session opens Sign in. Play as guest exists but is visually secondary. The entrance illustration depicts scenic road driving rather than the actual overhead circuit view.
findings.impact: The first decision concerns identity before the player understands the game.
findings.recommendation: Give first-time players a prominent route into a suitable starter race, brief control guidance and a later contextual sign-in request. Use art that sets accurate racing expectations.

findings.title: Protect unapplied preferences
findings.observed: A local state probe changed staged camera speed-zoom strength from 0.30 to 0.11, navigated Settings to Garage to Settings, and returned to 0.30 without a warning. This probe changed the draft property, not a simulated pointer gesture.
findings.impact: Players can believe they configured the game while their change was discarded.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the draft until an explicit choice or present Apply / Discard / Stay on departure. Indicate unsaved changes and disable Apply when unchanged.

findings.title: Separate empty, offline and failure states
findings.observed: The isolated disconnected track list says No tracks found and directs the player to filters/search. Offline Store presents access unavailable, sign-in, refresh and a separate unavailable message.
findings.impact: The suggested recovery may not address the cause and leaves a large unhelpful screen.
findings.recommendation: Use distinct no-match, no-download, offline and service-error states with one appropriate recovery action and useful retained content.

findings.title: Prioritise the repeat-race loop
findings.observed: Normal results already show Race Again, but Continue is the filled yellow action. Secondary results use Tracks while the main navigation names the destination Race.
findings.impact: The emphasis encourages another results page and makes destination names less predictable.
findings.recommendation: Make Race Again the leading action for ordinary time attack. Retain optional lap, histogram, reward and competition views, with consistent destination names.

findings.title: Clarify Garage selection and part semantics
findings.observed: The car gallery uses a generic SELECT action; confirming reveals car-specific tools. Tuning displays hood, aero, rims and body-kit choices.
findings.impact: Players must learn the preview/confirmed distinction and may expect performance changes from Tuning.
findings.recommendation: Use Select car and persistent confirmed-car feedback. Make the selected car and car-specific tool context clear. Consider Parts or Body parts for the current Tuning contents, or state the real effect precisely.

findings.title: Differentiate icon meanings and return actions
findings.observed: Track cards show a favorite star and a rating star. Circular-arrow controls denote different reset/refresh actions across the UI. Full track detail uses X to return to browsing.
findings.impact: Small, similar controls create avoidable interpretation work on touch.
findings.recommendation: Use distinct favorite/rating symbols, clear reset-view/reset-appearance labels where consequences differ, and consistent Back versus Close behavior. Audit Escape and Android Back with real input before claiming support.

findings.title: Improve compact-screen hierarchy and accessibility
findings.observed: At 960x540 the layout fits, but metadata, descriptions and muted labels shrink with the logical 1280x720 canvas. Many dark panels sit over dark workshop art.
findings.impact: Geometric fit does not establish comfortable phone reading or physical touch size.
findings.recommendation: Improve critical metadata size and surface separation, reduce redundant copy, add scalable text and verify physical touch targets. Preserve strong typography and restrained yellow emphasis.

findings.title: Make the next achievable goal visible
findings.observed: The achievement collection has clear medal progress, while the empty Trophy Wall is primarily an empty environment plus the collection action.
findings.impact: Players can inspect progress without immediately knowing what worthwhile goal is close.
findings.recommendation: Use the Trophy Room or a small contextual cue to surface one nearby unlock and the activity that earns it. Preserve the deliberately simple collection header and full collection access.

findings.title: Use a consistent motion policy
findings.observed: Menu slides, vertical race-mode changes, Garage camera movement and newspaper curl create a rich motion vocabulary. No reduced-motion preference was found in Settings.
findings.impact: Frequent navigation may feel slower or uncomfortable to some players; this remains a usability hypothesis.
findings.recommendation: Keep signature flourishes, make routine transitions brief and interruptible, and offer reduced motion.

proposed_sequence: Resolve UXR03 and UXR04, then label mode navigation.
Review the first-session route into a starter race.
Unify destination names, icon roles, selection and primary-action emphasis.
Polish compact-screen legibility and goal presentation; add reduced motion.

tasks: Start a first race without help.
Find Weekly Rivalry and return to Free Race.
Choose a car, customise it and return to racing.
Find an achievement and explain its next requirement.
Change one setting, leave and explain what was saved.
Recover from a no-match search and a disconnected catalogue.
proposed_validation.participants: A small formative study with approximately 5-8 unfamiliar players is a proposed next step, not a statistically conclusive sample.
